data.note:
Mist call: I over-weighted bright coarse tubulin/actin texture and contraction as microtubule stabilization, and overruled a weak split NSC vote.

Lesson: NSC similarities were low ~0.43-0.52 with split Protein degradation/Eg5/DNA replication votes - weak evidence I should have trusted less for a rare class. Cholesterol-lowering by HMG-CoA reductase inhibition PMID 3076125 can secondarily remodel cytoskeleton because mevalonate controls cytoskeleton organization and morphology PMID 8482726, mimicking bundling/contraction at 5-15 uM.

Next time: when atlas similarities are low and split, keep Cholesterol-lowering alive and seek low-dose actin/cell-shape dose response rather than committing to stabilizers on texture alone.

reflection.text:
Unblinded compound is mevinolin/lovastatin, an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor developed as a cholesterol-lowering agent (PMID 3076125) in the same pharmacologic class as simvastatin (PMID 30422514). I concluded Microtubule stabilizers at p=0.60 on the basis of extreme tub_glcm_contrast z=+66.8 at 15 uM (e3) and +24.8 at 5 uM (e7) plus the microscopist stabilizer call (e5). In retrospect those texture spikes reflected secondary cytoskeletal remodeling downstream of mevalonate depletion, which is known to control cytoskeleton organization and cell morphology (PMID 8482726).

The warning signs were in e4/e9 and e10-e12, which I overruled. Both atlas comparisons voted Protein degradation (1/2 then 2/4) with k-neighbours split across Eg5 inhibitors, Microtubule destabilizers and Actin disruptors and low similarities 0.43-0.52, never a stabilizer majority, while all three dose-response tests were non-monotonic and non-significant (tub_glcm_contrast rho=-0.20 p=0.8, tub_mean rho=-0.20 p=0.8, frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.40 p=0.6). The 50 uM well (e8) with nuc_solidity z=-192.5 and low cell counts at high doses signaled pleiotropic collapse rather than classic stabilization-associated mitotic arrest, consistent with statin cellular effects independent of cholesterol lowering (PMID 12371961).

Acquisition compounded the error: I sampled only 1.5, 5, 15 and 50 uM with no low-dose or replicate wells to define specificity, and weighted a single visual bundling impression over quantitative non-monotonicity. The reference atlas contains no Cholesterol-lowering class so NSC voting could never return the truth; a direct HMG-CoA/mevalonate rescue test was needed instead of further texture features.
what_was_right: Detected potent bioactivity with extreme act/tub texture z-scores (+22 to +66) at 5-15 uM (e3, e7) and early actin changes plus multinucleate proxy at 1.5 uM (e2), correctly rejecting inactivity.
Recorded reduced density and severe nuclear distortion at 50 uM with nuc_solidity z=-192.5 (e8) and low counts (69-242 cells at high doses), indicating pleiotropic/toxic component.
Atlas comparisons (e4, e9) correctly withheld support for stabilizers, voting Protein degradation and splitting neighbours among Eg5, destabilizers and actin disruptors with low similarity.
what_was_wrong: Misread tub_glcm_contrast +66.8 (e3) and +24.8 (e7) plus act_glcm_contrast/act_std as direct microtubule bundling/stabilization, when statin-driven mevalonate loss remodels cytoskeleton secondarily.
Over-weighted describe_phenotype stabilizer candidate (e5) and upgraded stabilizers from 0.40 to 0.60 despite contradicting NSC votes (e4, e9).
Ignored three non-significant negative dose-response results (e10-e12) that contradicted expected monotonic stabilizer bundling and mitotic arrest.
Acquired only mid-to-high doses (1.5-50 uM, 4 wells) with no low-dose 0.015-0.5 uM baseline or replicates, missing chance to see metabolic-class dose separation from direct cytoskeletal drugs.

Simvastatin exemplifies the statin HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor class shared with lovastatin.

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Cholesterol-lowering**.

## Reflection

Unblinded compound is mevinolin/lovastatin, an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor developed as a cholesterol-lowering agent (PMID 3076125) in the same pharmacologic class as simvastatin (PMID 30422514). I concluded Microtubule stabilizers at p=0.60 on the basis of extreme tub_glcm_contrast z=+66.8 at 15 uM (e3) and +24.8 at 5 uM (e7) plus the microscopist stabilizer call (e5). In retrospect those texture spikes reflected secondary cytoskeletal remodeling downstream of mevalonate depletion, which is known to control cytoskeleton organization and cell morphology (PMID 8482726).

The warning signs were in e4/e9 and e10-e12, which I overruled. Both atlas comparisons voted Protein degradation (1/2 then 2/4) with k-neighbours split across Eg5 inhibitors, Microtubule destabilizers and Actin disruptors and low similarities 0.43-0.52, never a stabilizer majority, while all three dose-response tests were non-monotonic and non-significant (tub_glcm_contrast rho=-0.20 p=0.8, tub_mean rho=-0.20 p=0.8, frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.40 p=0.6). The 50 uM well (e8) with nuc_solidity z=-192.5 and low cell counts at high doses signaled pleiotropic collapse rather than classic stabilization-associated mitotic arrest, consistent with statin cellular effects independent of cholesterol lowering (PMID 12371961).

Acquisition compounded the error: I sampled only 1.5, 5, 15 and 50 uM with no low-dose or replicate wells to define specificity, and weighted a single visual bundling impression over quantitative non-monotonicity. The reference atlas contains no Cholesterol-lowering class so NSC voting could never return the truth; a direct HMG-CoA/mevalonate rescue test was needed instead of further texture features.

What was right:
- Detected potent bioactivity with extreme act/tub texture z-scores (+22 to +66) at 5-15 uM (e3, e7) and early actin changes plus multinucleate proxy at 1.5 uM (e2), correctly rejecting inactivity.
- Recorded reduced density and severe nuclear distortion at 50 uM with nuc_solidity z=-192.5 (e8) and low counts (69-242 cells at high doses), indicating pleiotropic/toxic component.
- Atlas comparisons (e4, e9) correctly withheld support for stabilizers, voting Protein degradation and splitting neighbours among Eg5, destabilizers and actin disruptors with low similarity.

What was wrong or missed:
- Misread tub_glcm_contrast +66.8 (e3) and +24.8 (e7) plus act_glcm_contrast/act_std as direct microtubule bundling/stabilization, when statin-driven mevalonate loss remodels cytoskeleton secondarily.
- Over-weighted describe_phenotype stabilizer candidate (e5) and upgraded stabilizers from 0.40 to 0.60 despite contradicting NSC votes (e4, e9).
- Ignored three non-significant negative dose-response results (e10-e12) that contradicted expected monotonic stabilizer bundling and mitotic arrest.
- Acquired only mid-to-high doses (1.5-50 uM, 4 wells) with no low-dose 0.015-0.5 uM baseline or replicates, missing chance to see metabolic-class dose separation from direct cytoskeletal drugs.

Proposed next experiment: Mevalonate rescue imaging: repeat dose curve with and without co-supplemented mevalonate plus a direct tubulin polymerization assay and cholesterol-pathway readout versus paclitaxel control to test secondary cytoskeletal remodeling versus direct microtubule stabilization.
